title: DRAFT: Decoupling Backpropagation from Pre-trained Backbone for Efficient Transformer Fine-Tuning on Edge
problem: Efficient fine-tuning of pre-trained Transformers on resource-constrained edge devices, where backpropagation through massive backbone weights incurs high computational cost and memory overhead.
motivation: Transformer fine-tuning requires expensive backpropagation through pre-trained weights; edge devices with limited compute and memory need efficient alternatives to enable on-device personalization.
method: DRAFT framework decouples backpropagation via Feedback Decoupling Approximation (FDA) into two pathways: trainable adapter pathway and sparse ternary Bypass Network (BPN). A reconfigurable DRAFT accelerator features lightweight sparse gather networks and dynamic workflows to exploit sparsity and data parallelism inherent to FDA.
key_novelty: Algorithm-hardware co-design decoupling backpropagation from backbone weights via FDA dual-pathway approximation, reducing BP overhead while maintaining accuracy.
contributions: FDA algorithm that decouples backpropagation into low-complexity adapter and sparse ternary BPN pathways
DRAFT accelerator with reconfigurable design featuring sparse gather networks
4.9x speedup and 4.2x energy efficiency improvement over baseline fine-tuning methods
Negligible accuracy loss across multiple fine-tuning tasks
primary_theme: Edge-efficient transformer fine-tuning via backpropagation decoupling
